item.title: Iranian official says 'illegal routes' in Strait of Hormuz to soon be blocked
item.description:
DUBAI, Oct 7 (Reuters) - Transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz deemed illegal by Iran will soon be closed, an adviser to the Revolutionary Guards' Commander told the semi-officialFars News Agency on Wednesday, referring to the southern pathway hugging Oman's coast.

Mohammadreza Naqdi said these "few routes" had been created by blasting and damaging some of the rocky passages in the strategic waterway and were used by "small boats smuggling oil and transferring it to tankers", challenging the narrative that Gulf oil exports are regaining pre-war levels.

item.title: Israeli fire kills Palestinian in West Bank settler clash
item.description:
A Palestinian man was killed and nine people were injured during an Israeli settler attack followed by army intervention in an occupied West Bank village on Wednesday, according to the mayor and the Palestinian health ministry.

The Palestinian health ministry said 44-year-old Ali al-Bazzari died and nine others were injured "as a result of an assault by occupation forces and settlers" on the village of Burqa, north of Nablus in the northern West Bank.

item.title: Turkey sending technical, defensive support to Saudi Arabia to help fight Houthis, officials say
item.description:
By Tuvan Gumrukcu and Timour Azhari

ANKARA/RIYADH, Oct 7 (Reuters) - Turkey is sending mainly defensive and technical support to Saudi Arabia to help it fight Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis, two officials said on Wednesday, after the NATO member and Pakistan pledged to act on the collective defence commitment of their newly formed alliance.

item.title: More than 200,000 people displaced since fighting in Yemen began, says UN agency
item.description:
By Olivia Le Poidevin

GENEVA, Oct 7 (Reuters) - More than 200,000 people have been displaced from their homes since fighting inYemen began in recent weeks, according to data released on Wednesday by the United Nations' International Organization for Migration.

IOM described the crisis sparked by renewed fighting between the Iran-backedHouthi groupand Saudi-backed governmentforces in Yemen as alarming, with displacement figures surging from 76,000 in mid-September to more than 200,000 as of Wednesday — nearly all of whom fled since fighting began in early September.

item.title: Mayor of Turkey's secular stronghold Izmir joins Erdogan's party
item.description:
By Ece Toksabay and Huseyin Hayatsever

ANKARA, Oct 7 (Reuters) - The mayor of Izmir, Turkey's third-largest city and a bastion of its secular opposition, joined President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party (AKP) on Wednesday, amid a crackdown on the opposition in which dozens of mayors have been jailed.

Cemil Tugay, elected mayor in 2024 as a candidate of the opposition Republican People's Party (CHP) before quitting in June, formally joined the AKP at a ceremony in Ankara, handing Erdogan's party the mayoralty of a city it has never managed to win at the ballot box.

item.title: Rubio says US, Greece to jointly combat security threats
item.description:
ATHENS, Oct 7 - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that "strong and model NATO ally" Greece and the United States are launching new counterterrorism information sharing between their law enforcement agencies.

During an official visit to Athens,Rubio said Greece was particularly exposed to the threats posed by mass migration and human trafficking.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis claim new attacks on Saudi airports as conflict deepens
item.description:
The Houthis claimed a flurry of attacks on Saudi targets on Wednesday including firing a ballistic missile at Riyadh airport, as the group battles for territory in Yemen against government forces supported by the kingdom.

The Houthis, who control most of northwest Yemen, captured swathes of coastal land from Yemen's pro-government forces last month after the country's civil war reignited in July.

The fighting has displaced more than 200,000 people within the country, the United Nations said Wednesday.

item.title: IEA to meet Wednesday over proposed release of oil, diesel stocks, two EU diplomats say
item.description:
By Kate Abnett

BRUSSELS, Oct 7 (Reuters) - The International Energy Agency will hold an informal meeting on Wednesday to discuss a proposed release of oil and diesel stocks, two EU diplomats said, as details regarding the exact volume and composition under the plan remained unclear.

Record-high diesel prices have turned the fuel, which underpins trucking, agriculture and industry, into a global political and economic concern.

item.title: Israelis mark three years since October 7 as Palestinians mourn Gaza's destruction
item.description:
By Rami Amichay and Mahmoud Issa

KFAR AZA, Israel/GAZA, Oct 7 (Reuters) - Israelis gathered in silence on Wednesday in a kibbutz near the Gaza border that was overrun by Hamas militants on October 7 three years ago, mourning victims of attacks that set off Israel's assault in Gaza and plunged the Middle East into war.

In the Gaza Strip, devastated by two years of Israeli bombardment, Palestinians sheltering among the ruins of destroyed cities recalled life before a war that displaced nearly the entire population and tore apart families.

item.title: Mourning, war and elections as Israel marks October 7
item.description:
Israel marked the third anniversary of Hamas's October 7 attack on Wednesday with silent tributes, new strikes on Gaza and intense political debate, weeks before elections in which the country's deadliest day will be front and centre.

At the site of the Nova music festival, where Hamas militants in trucks and paragliders opened fire around dawn on October 7, 2023, family members bowed their heads quietly -- although at least one instead put on techno music in tribute to the fallen.

item.title: Pacific nations insist world must increase efforts to meet global warming limit
item.description:
By Peter Hobson

NADI, Fiji, Oct 7 (Reuters) - Global governments must increase efforts to reduce emissions because the planet is "hurtling past" a critical temperature target that would restrain sea level rises and extreme weather, delegates at a major climate conference in Fiji said on Wednesday.

Pacific nations, which are among the world's most vulnerable to climate change, are trying to lock their priorities into global climate negotiations at the ministerial meeting in Fiji, a precursor to the COP31 forum in Turkey in November.

item.title: Houthis attack Aden airport as fighting intensifies in Yemen
item.description:
By Enas Alashray, Mohammed Ghobari and Timour Azhari

Oct 7 (Reuters) - Yemen's Houthis attacked Aden's international airport with ballistic missiles and explosive-laden drones on Wednesday, the country's Transport Ministry said, as fighting between the Iran-aligned group and Saudi-backed government forces intensified.

Battles have focused in recent days on areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping route that has become more crucial for energy exports since the conflict between the US and Iran restricted trade through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Transcript of US Vice President Vance interview in Alaska
item.description:
By Jacob Bogage

FAIRBANKS, Alaska, Oct 6 (Reuters) - US Vice President JD Vance gave an exclusive interview to Reuters on Monday while campaigning in Alaska, a state that has emerged as a key battleground in the November elections that will determine control of Congress.

This transcript of the interview, which took place after a rally at Fairbanks International Airport for Republican US Senator Dan Sullivan, has been edited lightly for length and clarity.

Jacob Bogage, Reuters:

item.title: Exclusive-In interview, US Vice President Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war
item.description:
By Jacob Bogage

FAIRBANKS, Alaska, Oct 6 (Reuters) - US Vice President JD Vance said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries’ seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how Tehran makes decisions in negotiations.

item.title: Trump says nobody knows who is running Iran
item.description:
By Gram Slattery and Kanishka Singh

WASHINGTON, Oct 6 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that nobody knew who was running Iranduring the US-Israeli war with Iran, now in its eighth month.

QUOTES AND DETAILS:

• "Their leaders are gone, their second group of leaders are gone, and the biggest problem I have is nobody knows who the hell is running the country," Trump said.

• Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said on Sunday Washington knows very well who their counterpart is in Iran and how the decision-making system in Iran works.
